name: Guardians of the Whills
overview: The Guardians of the Whills are an ancient order sworn to protect the Temple of the Kyber on the holy moon of Jedha. Distinct from but historically linked to the Jedi, the Guardians integrate martial discipline with deep spiritual faith in the Force, even though many members are not themselves Force-sensitive. Under the Empire, with the Temple occupied and the pilgrimage economy destroyed, the order is nearly extinct — but a few Guardians remain, willing to rise against Imperial arrogance.
short_descriptor: Nearly extinct. What remains is on Jedha, and Jedha is occupied. Martial tradition with Force sensitivity — not Jedi, something older. If you encounter them, they're protecting something. Respect that.

how_they_operate.heading: THE TEMPLE OF THE KYBER
how_they_operate.text: The order is structured around the Temple of the Kyber on Jedha, with individual Guardians sworn to its protection through an unbroken chain of guardianship stretching back millennia.

how_they_operate.heading: MEMBERSHIP AND TRAINING
how_they_operate.text: Membership does not require Force sensitivity — faith and martial discipline are the entry requirements, and the lightbow is the traditional weapon, hand-built by each Guardian. Training integrates combat technique with spiritual practice so thoroughly that even non-Force-sensitive Guardians fight with uncanny intuition.

how_they_operate.heading: THE DISCIPLES
how_they_operate.text: The Disciples of the Whills, a related but distinct group, maintain the charitable infrastructure — orphanages, austere communal living, service to pilgrims.

how_they_operate.heading: UNDER OCCUPATION
how_they_operate.text: Under Imperial occupation, the surviving handful of Guardians operate without formal hierarchy, coordinating through personal contact and trusted intermediaries among Jedha City's faithful population.

witness_statement.text: Saw the blind one in the market square. Three stormtroopers hassling a pilgrim over papers. He walked straight into the middle of it with that staff and just stood there. Didn't say a word. They left. I asked the pilgrim what happened and she said 'He does that.' Like it was weather.
witness_statement.source: Offworld pilgrim, Jedha City holy quarter

secondary: Protection of the Temple of the Kyber and its legacy
Preservation of spiritual knowledge and practice
Resistance to Imperial desecration of Jedha
Care for the orphans and dispossessed of Jedha City
motivations.notes: The Guardians' motivation is rooted in millennia of sworn duty to the Temple and the Force. Unlike the Jedi, this duty does not require Force sensitivity — faith and martial discipline suffice. The Imperial occupation has transformed their protective mission from guarding a functioning temple to preserving what fragments of tradition survive.

strategic: Preserve the spiritual legacy and knowledge of the Disciples of the Whills and the Temple of the Kyber
Resist Imperial exploitation of Jedha's kyber crystal resources
Maintain the order's existence and traditions until the Temple can be restored
operational: Protect remaining practitioners, orphans, and pilgrims in Jedha City from Imperial brutality and criminal exploitation
Guard whatever kyber crystal deposits remain hidden from Imperial mining operations
Maintain the charitable traditions of the Disciples — orphanages, austere living, service to the community

avoided: Open military confrontation — the Guardians lack the numbers and resources for sustained combat
Assassination — the order's spiritual foundation forbids murder, though martial self-defense is a core practice
methods.notes: The Guardians' traditional weapon is the lightbow, a hand-made ranged weapon, though some have adopted more modern arms. Their martial talents are integrated into their faith — combat is a form of spiritual expression and understanding of the Force. In the current era, their methods are necessarily those of the powerless: hiding, protecting in small ways, and waiting.

strengths: Millennia of accumulated spiritual and martial knowledge passed through an unbroken chain of guardianship
Deep integration of combat discipline with Force awareness — even non-Force-sensitive Guardians fight with uncanny intuition
Intimate knowledge of Jedha City's ancient architecture, subterranean levels, and hidden passages
Moral authority among Jedha's faithful population, who revere the Guardians even under Imperial occupation
Austerity and self-sufficiency — Guardians craft essentials from discarded materials and need almost nothing to survive
weaknesses: The order is reduced to a handful of active members after the Imperial occupation caused the majority to abandon Jedha or renounce their vows.
The Guardians possess no institutional funding, material reserves, or connections to external support networks of any kind.
The Temple of the Kyber — the order's central purpose and sacred charge — is under permanent Imperial military control, rendering the core mission unachievable through direct action.
Jedha is accessible only through circuitous hyperspace routes, and Imperial travel restrictions further limit offworld contact, isolating the order from potential allies or resources.
The civilian population the Guardians serve and protect on Jedha lacks surplus resources, leaving the order without a sustainable material support base.

behavior_under_threat.low: Observe and avoid. Guardians blend into the civilian population of Jedha City, relying on the anonymity of monk's robes and the city's crowded streets.
behavior_under_threat.medium: Activate knowledge of the city's hidden passages and subterranean levels to move people and objects out of danger. Martial readiness increases among remaining Guardians.
behavior_under_threat.high: Direct confrontation becomes unavoidable. Guardians fight with lightbows and improvised weapons, using the Temple's architecture and their superior knowledge of the terrain to maximize advantage against superior numbers.
behavior_under_threat.critical: The remaining Guardians make their stand. With nothing left to lose and everything sacred at stake, they fight to the death or scatter into the desert wastelands beyond Jedha City to preserve what knowledge they can carry.

alert_escalation.notes: The Guardians have no formal military communication structure. Information passes through personal contact, trusted intermediaries among the faithful, and the intuitive awareness that some Guardians develop through their spiritual practice. Escalation is slow because the chain is personal and the members are few.

tension_patterns: The Guardians' founding oath binds them to protect the Temple of the Kyber, which is now under permanent Imperial military occupation, leaving the oath's practical application undefined.

Any Force-sensitive individual arriving on Jedha risks drawing Inquisitorius attention to the moon's surviving Force practitioners, creating a direct conflict between the order's recruitment needs and its survival.

Remaining kyber crystal deposits beneath Jedha's ruins are sought by Imperial mining operations, Rebel Alliance procurement agents, and black market dealers simultaneously, while the Guardians lack the numbers to secure more than a fraction of known sites.

Offworld parties periodically offer surviving Guardians passage, resources, or protection in exchange for knowledge of the Temple's hidden chambers and subterranean passages, testing individual commitment to the order's secrecy obligations.

The collapse of Jedha's pilgrimage economy under Imperial occupation eliminated the Guardians' traditional support base, leaving the remaining members dependent on charity from a civilian population that itself lacks surplus resources.

mcguffin_interest.notes: The Guardians care deeply about Force artifacts, kyber crystals, and relics of the Temple and Jedha's spiritual heritage. Persons of interest include Force-sensitive individuals who might join the order and pilgrims who carry knowledge of other traditions. Material wealth, weapons, and technology hold no appeal.

relationship_notes.rebel_alliance: The Alliance and the Guardians share an enemy but not a cause. Some Jedha insurgents have Alliance ties, and individual Guardians may assist Rebel operatives, but the order's mission is spiritual, not political.
relationship_notes.imperial_military: The Imperial garrison on Jedha mines kyber crystals, brutalizes civilians, and occupies the Temple. The Guardians view this as desecration on every level.
relationship_notes.inquisitorius: The Inquisitors represent the most direct threat to any remaining Force-sensitive Guardians. Their presence on Jedha would mean the end of the order.
relationship_notes.black_sun: Criminal elements in Jedha City prey on pilgrims with fake artifacts and black market operations. The Guardians oppose this exploitation but lack the power to stop it.

prominent_figures.name: Chirrut Imwe
prominent_figures.notes: A blind Guardian who demonstrates extraordinary martial skill guided by faith in the Force. His combat abilities exemplify the order's integration of spiritual practice with fighting technique. He is not confirmed Force-sensitive, yet trusts the Force to guide his actions.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Chirrut is blind, unarmed by modern standards, and the most dangerous person on any street in Jedha City. His faith is operational — it produces results that defy tactical analysis. Do not underestimate him because he smiles.
prominent_figures.wants: To protect the people of Jedha and preserve the spiritual legacy of the Temple of the Kyber through personal action and unwavering faith.
prominent_figures.secret: Knows the location of hidden chambers beneath the Temple that the Imperial mining operation has not yet discovered. Will die before revealing them.

behavior.under_pressure: Becomes calmer. His mantra — 'I am one with the Force, the Force is with me' — is not decoration; it is a combat focus technique that measurably improves his response time.
behavior.when_losing: Does not acknowledge losing. His faith precludes despair. He will fight, pray, and smile through any situation until it resolves or he dies.
behavior.loyalty: To the Force, to the Temple, and to Baze Malbus — in that order. The order itself is secondary to the faith it represents.
behavior.tells: His staff shifts from a walking aid to a combat grip several seconds before visible threats materialize. Whether this is Force sensitivity or extraordinary hearing is unknown.

useful_to_players: Intimate knowledge of Jedha City's streets, hidden passages, and subterranean levels
Martial skill sufficient to neutralize stormtrooper patrols without a blaster
His moral authority among Jedha's faithful population can open doors no weapon can
hooks: Chirrut has been seen walking the same route past the Imperial garrison every morning for a week — either he is praying or he is scouting
A pilgrim arrived on Jedha carrying something Chirrut said he has been waiting for. Neither will say what it is.

prominent_figures.name: Baze Malbus
prominent_figures.notes: Once among the most devoted Guardians, Baze lost his faith under the weight of Imperial occupation. He remains on Jedha as a heavily-armed protector, representing the crisis of belief that the occupation has inflicted on the order.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Baze lost his faith but kept his skills and added a heavy repeating blaster. He follows Chirrut because someone has to keep the blind monk alive. Pragmatic, heavily armed, and more dangerous than he looks — which is saying something.
prominent_figures.wants: To protect Chirrut Imwe and, through him, whatever remains worth protecting on Jedha — even if he no longer believes in the spiritual framework that once gave those things meaning.
prominent_figures.secret: His crisis of faith is not complete. He still performs fragments of Guardian rituals when he thinks no one is watching.

behavior.under_pressure: Puts himself between the threat and Chirrut. His tactical instincts are Guardian-trained but his weapons loadout is purely practical.
behavior.when_losing: Fights harder. His lack of faith means he has no expectation of divine intervention — survival depends on firepower and aggression.
behavior.loyalty: To Chirrut Imwe personally. The Temple, the order, the Force — he has given up on all of it. Chirrut is the last thing holding him to Jedha.
behavior.tells: Watches Chirrut constantly. If Chirrut moves toward danger, Baze is already repositioning to cover him before the threat is visible to anyone else.

useful_to_players: Heavy weapons expertise and Guardian combat training make him one of the most capable fighters on Jedha
Knows Guardian martial techniques and Temple architecture from his years as a devoted member
His pragmatic worldview makes him easier to negotiate with than the faith-bound Chirrut
hooks: Baze was seen purchasing power cells in quantities that suggest he is preparing for something bigger than street patrols
A former Guardian reached out to Baze asking for help leaving Jedha. Baze has not responded. Chirrut does not know about the message.

source_material_notes: Dawn of Rebellion provides the primary treatment of Jedha and the Guardians of the Whills across pages 41-42, including the Temple of the Kyber, Jedha City, Imperial occupation, the Disciples of the Whills, and the Guardians' martial traditions. The Nexus of Power (Worlds Strong in the Force) sourcebook covers Jedha-adjacent Force traditions but does not contain specific entries for 'Whills' or 'Jedha' in the available PDF. Chirrut Imwe and Baze Malbus are known from Rogue One rather than FFG sourcebooks.
